investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official events listing page (WordPress + 'Events Manager' plugin) and one event detail page. Also attempted the plugin's own public REST API root and its events endpoint directly (still an unauthenticated Level 1 GET) — the WordPress REST root (/wp-json/) is publicly readable and lists the plugin's namespace, but the events endpoint itself (/wp-json/events-manager/v1/events) returned HTTP 401 (rest_forbidden). No authentication bypass was attempted; the static HTML listing/detail pages, which are genuinely public, were used instead and were fully sufficient.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's official events listing page (https://huxleysneuewelt.de/en/events) immediately exposed 111 distinct upcoming event entries as fully server-rendered static HTML (WordPress 'Events Manager' plugin's grouped-list widget), grouped under month/year headings. One sampled event detail page directly stated a full date, start/doors time, and (via the page's own server-generated og:description meta tag) an explicit end time, plus ticketing via an external first-party-embedded Eventim link. The plugin's own REST API events endpoint was also tried directly and found to require authentication (401) — a legitimate access-control boundary, not bypassed. No JSON-LD MusicEvent, ICS, Fourvenues, or Sanity signal was present on the sampled pages (the site's JSON-LD is generic Yoast SEO WebPage/Organization graph only, no per-event schema); none was needed, since the static HTML itself fully answered the investigation question.

venue_reference: Huxleys Neue Welt (mid-size concert hall, Hasenheide, Neukölln, Berlin)

identity.notes: The retained listing page's own <title> reads 'Events - Huxleys Neue Welt'. Independently, the retained event detail page's own footer states 'Huxleys Neue Welt / Hasenheide 107 – 113 / D-10967 Berlin' with a Google Maps link — matching the venue's known Neukölln/Hasenheide-park address — a second, distinct retained artifact confirming identity.

site_classification.platform: WordPress with the 'Events Manager' plugin (confirmed via the public /wp-json/ REST root listing an 'events-manager/v1' namespace with an /events route) and Yoast SEO. The events listing page server-renders a grouped list of upcoming events as static HTML; each event's own detail page states a full date/start/doors time in visible text and an explicit end time only in its server-generated og:description meta tag. The plugin's own REST events endpoint requires authentication and was not used. No JSON-LD MusicEvent, ICS, Fourvenues, or Sanity signal was present.

title.notes: The listing row's own YEBBA and the detail page's own /og:title ('YEBBA - Huxleys Neue Welt') both state the title directly.

start_date.notes: The event's own detail page directly states the full date in one place: 'Date: Wed 02.09.2026' — no combination with surrounding context needed for this field, even though the listing page's own grouped rows (day+month only, year from a month/year heading) would require a DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT combination if the listing page alone were used.

time.value: 20:00 (Europe/Berlin, floating local — no explicit UTC offset stated anywhere on this source)
time.notes: The detail page directly states 'Start: 20:00' (and separately 'Doors: 19:00'); the same page's own server-generated og:description meta tag independently states 'Wed 02.09.2026 @ 20:00 - 22:30', corroborating the same start clock time. Unlike the AEG-operated Berlin venues and Columbiahalle already investigated in this trial, no ICS or other UTC-offset-qualified field exists anywhere on this source — recorded honestly as FLOATING_LOCAL, not upgraded to a UTC instant.

end.value: 22:30 (Europe/Berlin, floating local — same no-offset caveat as time)
end.notes: The detail page's own server-generated og:description meta tag directly states 'Wed 02.09.2026 @ 20:00 - 22:30' — the '22:30' is this source's own stated end time (not visible in the human-readable page body, which only shows Start/Doors, but genuinely present in the page's own retained markup, generated by the same plugin from its own internal event end-time field). Recorded as floating local, same as time.

venue_location.notes: Individual event listing rows/detail pages do not restate the venue name or address per event — this is the venue's own single-venue official site (every /event/ page is inherently this one venue), matching the same NOT_PRESENT-per-record treatment already used for razzmatazz-barcelona-01 and verti-music-hall-berlin-01 (resolved via source_id, not a per-record field).

source_record_id.notes: The event's own detail-page URL path segment (date + slug, e.g. '/en/event/2026-09-02-yebba') is the site's own canonical, directly-stated permalink for that specific occurrence — the same documented URL-slug stable-identifier strategy already used for moog-barcelona-01/LAV and for the AEG-operated Berlin venues already investigated in this trial.

event_url.notes: The listing row's own detail-page link, and the detail page's own canonical <link rel="canonical"> tag, both state this directly.

price.notes: No first-party price is shown on either the listing page or the sampled event detail page — only an outbound ticket-purchase link to Eventim (the venue's own embedded ticketing partner, not a first-party price field on this source itself).

blockers.description: The 'end' field's value is only directly retrievable from the detail page's og:description meta tag text (a loosely-structured 'HH:MM - HH:MM' substring), not from a dedicated machine-readable field — a future collector would need a small, deterministic text-extraction rule for this specific meta tag, not a generic schema parse. This exact rule is now implemented and offline-proven (ingestion/huxleys-neue-welt/observation-adapter.mjs's extractEndFromDetailPage()/enrichEndFromDetailPage(), tests/huxleys-neue-welt.test.mjs) — retained as context, not CRITICAL, and does not block activation.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from two independently retained artifacts (listing page title, and the detail page's own footer address).
acquisition_class STATIC_HTML, a resolved supported class, reached at Level 1 with no escalation needed.

A CONFIRMED public data path retained: the full 111-event listing page plus a sampled event detail page; the plugin's own REST events endpoint was correctly identified as PRIVATE/REJECTED (401) and not used.
title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE — the detail page states the full date directly, avoiding the need for the listing page's own month/year-heading combination.
end additionally PROVEN via the detail page's own server-generated og:description meta tag, a genuinely retained first-party field.
source_record_id PROVEN via the site's own slug+date permalink path, following the documented moog-barcelona-01/LAV precedent.

No unresolved CRITICAL blocker (only one MINOR blocker noting the og:description text-extraction rule needed for 'end').

Source re-verified live on 2026-08-26 (second-pass re-verification): a fresh, plain unauthenticated curl GET of the same events listing page and the same YEBBA detail page returned HTTP 200 with the same 111 grouped upcoming event entries and the same og:description end-time shape as the original sample — nothing materially changed since the original investigation; both fresh captures retained byte-faithfully as ev-events-listing-reverify-2026-08-26 and ev-event-detail-yebba-reverify-2026-08-26. A genuine, dependency-free, no-network offline test suite (tests/huxleys-neue-welt.test.mjs, 10 tests, all passing) now re-parses these retained fixtures and reproduces every claimed field (title incl. HTML-entity decoding, full date via this source's own detail-page URL slug, start/doors time, sold-out/cancelled status, and the og:description end-time extraction with a mismatched-date safety check) deterministically and offline, across the full retained 111-event listing plus the retained detail-page sample — gate 9/v1.2 offline-proof requirement now satisfied. Advanced from READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF to READY_FOR_ACTIVATION.
